screenshots.title: Sign up from the Lingry home screen
screenshots.altText: Lingry home screen with the Sign up tab open, showing email and password fields, a Sign up button, and a Sign up by Key option.
screenshots.purpose: Users can sign up from the Lingry home screen by entering an email, creating a password, and confirming it. A key-based sign-up option is also available for users who prefer wallet-key access.
screenshots.whatUserSees: The Lingry home screen is open with the Sign up tab selected. The form shows email address, password, and confirm password fields, plus Sign up, Continue with Google, and Sign up by Key options.
screenshots.whyStepMatters: This is the main account-creation entry point and shows that users can choose either the standard email/password flow or the wallet-key path.
screenshots.userAction: Enter an email address, create a password, confirm the password, then select Sign up. Users who prefer wallet-key access can select Sign up by Key instead.
screenshots.expectedResult: Lingry creates the wallet session and brings the user into the app.
screenshots.agentGuidance: Guide the user to choose the normal email sign-up path unless they specifically want wallet-key access. Never ask the user to paste a private key, password, or session token into chat.

screenshots.title: Save your login key
screenshots.altText: Lingry account screen showing a Save your login key panel with the key value redacted and a Copy button visible above the Word Stream.
screenshots.purpose: After creating an account, Lingry provides a wallet key for future login. Users should save this key securely before continuing, since it allows them to access the wallet again later.
screenshots.whatUserSees: The Lingry app shows a Save your login key panel near the top of the Word Stream. The login key field is present, the key value is redacted in this documentation screenshot, and a Copy button is available.
screenshots.whyStepMatters: This is the user's recovery and future-login credential, so it must be saved privately before they move on.
screenshots.userAction: Copy the login key and save it somewhere secure before continuing in Lingry.
screenshots.expectedResult: The user has a saved login key they can use to access the wallet again later.
screenshots.agentGuidance: Explain that this key must be treated like a wallet credential. Tell the user to save it privately and never paste it into chat, public docs, issue comments, or screenshots.

screenshots.title: Prompt for a new word
screenshots.altText: Lingry Prompt for New Word screen showing a concept prompt, an Invent From Prompt button, and a generated word suggestion with meaning and part-of-speech fields.
screenshots.purpose: Users can enter a prompt describing the idea or concept they want Lingry to turn into a new word. Lingry then uses that prompt to generate a more focused and personalized word suggestion.
screenshots.whatUserSees: The Prompt for New Word screen shows a text area containing a concept prompt, an Invent From Prompt button, a Coin It button, and a Generated Word panel with editable word, meaning, part of speech, etymology meaning, confidence, and status fields.
screenshots.whyStepMatters: This is where the user turns a plain-language concept into a focused Lingry word candidate before deciding whether it is worth coining.
screenshots.userAction: Type a concept or idea into the Prompt for New Word field, then select Invent From Prompt.
screenshots.expectedResult: Lingry generates a suggested word with meaning, part of speech, etymology meaning, confidence, and status details.
screenshots.agentGuidance: Help the user phrase the prompt clearly and specifically, then review the generated word details before recommending any coining or submission step.

screenshots.title: Generate a word with AI
screenshots.altText: Lingry AI Generate screen showing an Invent New Word button, Coin It button, and a generated word candidate with meaning, part of speech, etymology meaning, confidence, and status.
screenshots.purpose: The AI Generate tab automatically creates a new word idea for the user, including meaning and context. It gives users a fast way to discover and coin a new word with minimal input.
screenshots.whatUserSees: The AI Generate screen shows a generated word candidate, the Invent New Word and Coin It buttons, editable meaning and etymology fields, part of speech, confidence, and ready-to-post status.
screenshots.whyStepMatters: This gives users a fast path from opening Lingry to reviewing a coinable word candidate without having to write a prompt first.
screenshots.userAction: Open AI Generate and select Invent New Word to create a fresh word suggestion, then review or edit the generated details before selecting Coin It.
screenshots.expectedResult: Lingry shows a generated word candidate with meaning, part of speech, etymology meaning, confidence, and ready-to-post status.
screenshots.agentGuidance: Use this screen when the user wants a quick generated candidate. Encourage them to review and edit the meaning before preparing any coining request.

screenshots.title: View Lingry rankings
screenshots.altText: Lingry Rankings screen showing top trending word cards with creator handles, language flags, like counts, tip counts, and Sugar tip totals.
screenshots.purpose: Lingry Rankings shows top words and creators. Users can like favorite words and tip creators with Sugars, helping reward popular or meaningful word contributions.
screenshots.whatUserSees: The Lingry Rankings page shows refresh and scan information, a Stream button, a Refresh button, and Top Trending Words cards with rank numbers, language flags, creator handles, definitions, likes, tips, and Sugar totals.
screenshots.whyStepMatters: Rankings help users find active words and creators, then decide which contributions to support with likes or Sugar tips.
screenshots.userAction: Open Lingry Rankings, review the top trending words, then use like or tip actions when a word contribution is worth supporting.
screenshots.expectedResult: The user sees ranked words and creator activity ordered by likes and tips, with the latest refresh and scan context visible.
screenshots.agentGuidance: Use rankings to help the user discover popular words and creators. Explain that likes and tips are public contribution signals, and never claim a tip succeeded until the wallet/API confirms it.

screenshots.title: View wallet keys from the menu
screenshots.altText: Lingry Keys screen showing wallet address, public key, a masked private key field with a Show button, and redeem script details.
screenshots.purpose: From Menu > Show Keys, users can view their private key and save it for future logins. This key should be stored securely, since it provides access to the wallet.
screenshots.whatUserSees: The Keys screen shows account details, including the wallet address, public key, a private key field that remains masked in this documentation screenshot, a Show button, and redeem script information.
screenshots.whyStepMatters: This is where users can recover the credential needed for future wallet access, so it must be handled privately and stored securely.
screenshots.userAction: Open Menu, choose Show Keys, and only reveal or copy the private key when the user is in a private setting ready to store it securely.
screenshots.expectedResult: Lingry shows the wallet address, public key, masked private key field, and related wallet details so the user can save access information safely.
screenshots.agentGuidance: Warn the user that the private key controls wallet access. Never ask them to paste it into chat, screenshots, GitHub, ClawHub, logs, or support messages.

screenshots.title: Create an API session token for OpenClaw
screenshots.altText: Lingry API Session screen showing a redacted session token, an expiration date, Create API Session Token, Copy Token, and Revoke Token buttons.
screenshots.purpose: Menu: API Session. The API Session screen lets OpenClaw users create a Lingry session token for local OpenClaw tools. After signing in, the user opens Menu > API Session, creates a token, copies it, and adds it to their OpenClaw environment. The screen also shows the token expiration date, so users know when they need to refresh it. Lingry API session tokens are valid for about 30 days.
screenshots.whatUserSees: The API Session screen shows a redacted session-token field, an expiration timestamp, and Create API Session Token, Copy Token, and Revoke Token buttons. The page warns users to use the token only for a local OpenClaw skill and never paste it into chat, GitHub, shell history, or shared files.
screenshots.whyStepMatters: This connects Lingry browser authentication to local OpenClaw tooling without exposing the token to the agent. The expiration date tells the user when to refresh the token.
screenshots.userAction: Open Menu, choose API Session, create an API session token, copy it, and paste it only into the local OpenClaw environment file.
screenshots.expectedResult: The local OpenClaw tools can authenticate to Lingry until the displayed token expiration date, after which the user refreshes the token from the same screen.
screenshots.agentGuidance: Guide OpenClaw users to store the token only in their private local environment. Never ask them to paste the token into chat, GitHub, screenshots, shell history, logs, or shared files.
screenshots.command: Use the private terminal snippet in the paired screenshot documentation to write LINGRY_SESSION_TOKEN into $HOME/.openclaw/.env with 0600 permissions, then restart the OpenClaw gateway.

screenshots.title: Browse the Lingry word stream
screenshots.altText: Lingry Word Stream screen showing recent coined word cards with creator handles, flags, timestamps, meanings, Like and Tip controls.
screenshots.purpose: The Stream tab shows the Lingry word feed, where users can browse newly created words, read meanings, and discover community language activity.
screenshots.whatUserSees: The Word Stream shows a list of recent coined word cards with creator handles, language flags, timestamps, word names, meanings, Like and Tip controls, plus navigation to AI Generate and Prompt for New Word.
screenshots.whyStepMatters: This is the main discovery surface for community word activity and gives users a place to read, open, like, and tip public contributions.
screenshots.userAction: Open the Stream tab and scroll through the word cards to read new words, meanings, creators, and timestamps. Use Like or Tip when a contribution is worth supporting.
screenshots.expectedResult: The user sees recent Lingry words and can open, like, or tip public word contributions.
screenshots.agentGuidance: Use the Stream to help users discover recent word activity and explain meanings. Do not describe OpenClaw stream data as live or real-time; public agent reads use the latest completed snapshot.

screenshots.title: Send Sugars from the menu
screenshots.altText: Lingry Send screen showing balance, recipient address and amount fields, a fee field, Send button, and Reset button.
screenshots.purpose: From Menu > Send, users can transfer Sugars to another wallet address by entering the recipient, amount, and fee, then confirming the transaction.
screenshots.whatUserSees: The Send screen shows the current Sugar balance, recipient address and amount inputs, a fee input with recommended-fee placeholder text, a Send button, and a Reset button.
screenshots.whyStepMatters: This is the point where a user prepares an actual wallet transfer, so the recipient, amount, and fee must be reviewed carefully before submission.
screenshots.userAction: Open Menu, choose Send, enter the recipient wallet address, enter the Sugar amount and fee, then select Send only after reviewing the details.
screenshots.expectedResult: Lingry prepares the wallet transfer flow so the user can confirm and submit a Sugar transaction to the chosen recipient.
screenshots.agentGuidance: Help the user verify the recipient address, amount, and fee before sending. Never invent transaction status or claim a transfer succeeded until Lingry or the wallet confirms it.
